name: Main Bazaar and Brahma Temple
description: The lively core where the famous Brahma temple, crowded market lanes and colourful stalls converge. Days here are a swirl of pilgrims, cows, craft shops and rooftop cafes, with everything walkable and endless atmosphere, though quiet is in short supply.
bestFor: First-timers who want to be in the middle of everything
pros: Walk to temples, shops and food
Plenty of rooftop cafes with lake views

name: Ghats and Lakefront
description: The spiritual centre wrapped around Pushkar Lake and its fifty-two bathing ghats. This is the place for sunrise reflections, evening aarti and people-watching, with guesthouses and cafes overlooking the water, but strict rules and priest solicitation near the steps.
bestFor: Travellers drawn to ritual, reflection and sunset views over water
cons: Strict conduct rules at the ghats

name: Savitri Temple Hillside
description: The calmer southwestern edge rising toward the Savitri temple hill, dotted with laid-back guesthouses, gardens and yoga spots. It trades bazaar bustle for stillness, birdsong and easy access to the sunset climb, ideal for a slower, restorative stay away from crowds.
bestFor: Slow travellers, yoga seekers and anyone wanting quiet and greenery
cons: A walk from the main bazaar

name: Ajmer Road and Fairgrounds
description: The spread-out fringe along the Ajmer road and the vast Camel Fair grounds. Sleepy and open for most of the year, it transforms into a heaving festival hub each November. Handy for transport connections but removed from the town's day-to-day charm.
bestFor: Fair-season visitors and travellers needing easy road links to Ajmer
pros: Front-row seat for the Camel Fair
cons: Chaotic and pricey during the fair
